status_note: Reproduces on Spark 4.3.0, the latest release, in both ANSI modes; main not read. No issue for the missing error class: SPARK-54836 (open) asks for the timestamp's value in the same `ArithmeticException`.
title: Timestamp plus interval past the range raises a bare `ArithmeticException`, no error class
summary: Adding an interval to a timestamp near the end of the microsecond range raises a bare `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow` with no error class or SQLSTATE, where `timestampadd` and date arithmetic raise `DATETIME_OVERFLOW`. Clients that sort errors by class (sverify's runner maps classes to issues) cannot tell it from an internal failure.
handling: No workaround needed for results: the reference raises far earlier (`date_range`, 9999-12-31), so a guarded plan never reaches it. The fix upstream is to wrap the overflow in `DATETIME_OVERFLOW` in `DateTimeUtils.timestampAddInterval`.
found_by: the Spark characterization (#738): sverify_dev.probe_spark, probe timestamp-overflow
